A1.justification: Both PDFs describe KBQA-R1 and contain readable text, equations, tables, and figures. The comparison includes all material: v1 ends with references and biographies, while v3 adds Appendices A–B. Relocated content can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark results, component ablations, rejection-sampling experiments, inference-efficiency measurements, and training analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds frontier-agent comparisons, an adapted Search-R1 baseline, Hits@1 evaluations, and a knowledge-base transfer experiment.

M1.justification: The structured actions, three-tier RRCG validation, referenced rejection sampling, SFT warm-start, and GRPO training remain. The explicit per-turn SFT description and new pseudocode document the existing procedure. Clipping was already specified in v1, so the revised objective equation does not establish a new optimization procedure.

E1.justification: WebQSP, GrailQA, and GraphQuestions remain the question benchmarks. v3 Table 13 adds WebQSP evaluation after transferring the executor from Freebase to Wikidata, extending coverage to another knowledge-base environment. The 500-query frontier-agent subset does not introduce another dataset or task.

E2.justification: WebQSP gains RoG, GNN-RAG, and two SubgraphRAG variants in Table 4. New comparisons include four frontier models under SPARQL ReAct and the KBQA-R1 harness, GPT-based ToG/PoG in efficiency and Hits@1 comparisons, and an adapted Search-R1 baseline. These substantially expand the evaluated comparator set.

E3.justification: v3 introduces a fixed 500-query frontier-agent evaluation comprising 200 GrailQA, 200 WebQSP, and 100 GraphQ questions, with two interaction interfaces and turn/token measurements. It also adds Hits@1 evaluations alongside retained EM/F1 protocols. Reported GRPO top-p changes from 0.99 to 1.0; the PDFs do not establish whether existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds controls comparing frontier models with and without the structured harness, a Freebase-to-Wikidata transfer test, and a detailed GrailQA case contrasting KBQA-o1 failure with KBQA-R1 success. These extend the analysis beyond the original component ablations, sampling comparisons, and training dynamics, which remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report some main results with ± values without specifying repeated-run counts, seeds, or the uncertainty estimator. v3 adds no identifiable statistical reporting procedure. Changed GrailQA ± magnitudes are numerical result changes rather than a change in reporting practice.

E6.justification: Main KBQA-R1 mean F1 scores remain 83.4 on WebQSP, 86.1 on GrailQA, and 53.8 on GraphQ, but several GrailQA uncertainty values change, including overall F1 from ±0.3 to ±0.6. Extensive additional results include the 500-query averages of 79.0 for KBQA-R1 versus 71.6 for the strongest frontier harness, and 77.3 Hits@1 on Wikidata. These are newly reported evaluations, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: v1 Equation 3 gives an advantage-weighted log-policy objective with KL regularization; v3 Equation 2 replaces it with a clipped importance-ratio surrogate and explicitly defines the ratio. This revises the mathematical specification of optimization. No new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The central RL, RRS, and state-of-the-art performance claims remain. v3 adds an introductory contribution claiming over 70% fewer LLM calls than GPT-4-based ToG/PoG using an 8B backbone. It also narrows the introductory RRS contribution from preventing hallucinated logic to mitigating it during warm-start training.

C2.justification: v3 interprets the frontier comparisons as separating benefits of the harness from benefits of the learned policy. Appendix B.10 adds a specific causal argument about execution feedback and undetected KBQA-o1 errors. The impact statement newly discusses how incomplete or biased KB records constrain answer reliability; existing generalization and training-dynamics interpretations largely remain.

D1.justification: v3 adds code/project links, per-turn SFT sample construction, two algorithms, and explicit prompt-length, response-length, and six-turn limits. However, v1's learning rates, schedules, epoch counts, validation frequency, and checkpoint-selection rule disappear, despite v3 directing readers to Appendix B.3 for full hyperparameters. Hardware and KB infrastructure details are retained.

R1.justification: v3 expands discussion and citations to GNN-RAG, SubgraphRAG, DoG, Graph-R1, and HypergraphRAG, refining its positioning against graph retrieval and reasoning approaches. It removes v1's explicit attribution of RRS inspiration to STaR. Much of the original research positioning survives in Appendix A.

P1.justification: The introduction is substantially rewritten and methodological explanations are compressed. Detailed related work, experimental setup, efficiency discussion, and training-reward discussion move into appendices. New supplementary sections and an impact statement accompany removal of the biographies, substantially changing the document's organization.

P2.justification: v3 adopts a conference layout with single-column appendices and adds five tables, two algorithm blocks, an interaction-trace figure, and a comparative case-study panel. Existing comparison tables are expanded, Figure 1 gains topic-entity inputs, and the retained training-reward plot is relocated and enlarged. These are substantial display changes beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: The frontier models evaluated with the same harness, broader graph-method comparisons, and transfer test strengthen the empirical assessment beyond v1's retained headline results. Explicit algorithms and traces also improve inspectability. The net gain is limited by removal of previously documented training and model-selection settings, and an overbroad efficiency claim: Table 10 implies about 53% fewer calls than PoG on GrailQA, rather than the introduction's blanket over-70% claim.
